statement: Local homeomorphisms that commute with the full local centralizer, fix every actual global quotient map, and move points only over one compact local-centralizer quotient set extend over all original-operator translates by conjugation and by the identity elsewhere. This is a continuous injective group homomorphism with continuous restriction inverse, and compact parameter families extend jointly with their inverses even for noncompact quotients and arbitrary accumulation of translates. With two independent global quotient partitions, the identity path component of the quotient kernel is trivial.
depends_on: C42 exact equivariant-map evaluation homeomorphism with every source basepoint; C45 injectivity of the two real lifted quotient coordinates; C53 full global quotient family; C55 full local centralizer, its actual operator restriction kernel, properness, and exact local equivariance
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), infinite-operator zero-level comparison and relative frontier extension
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. Every transported local map is compared through actual L-equivariant maps hq. The original operator-stabilizer restriction kernel and every source/target cover are retained.
notes: The support saturation supplies a convergent basepoint subsequence from one compact set even though the whole quotient is noncompact. Small global L-elements align those basepoints; C42 then identifies the complete limit map as an actual global quotient or a constant. Pointwise quotient preservation forces the required frontier limit. Inverse moving sets coincide exactly, so the same proof gives joint inverse continuity. Operator-stabilizer independence proves the extension rule is well defined. Two quotient maps force a based kernel path to have zero target deck increments; their injective pair of real lifts then forces the path to be the identity. The theorem supplies localized relative perturbations in the zero/one-partition cases, but does not assert a fragmentation of the original transitive loop or a general C12 extension.
